title: Microcue attenuation notes and few-shot pruning experiments
content:
Notes-to-self / scratchpad: microcue attenuation project

Goal:
- Find simple prompt-library strategies to reduce brittle microcue-triggered failures across small/medium open models (rw-small, rw-medium-quant).
- Prefer tweaks that are cheap (prompt changes, exemplar reordering/pruning) vs infra changes (reranking, extra eval loop).

Background
- 'Microcues' = tiny lexical or structural signals in few-shot exemplars that the model latches onto (e.g., punctuation shape, phrasing pattern, label formatting) and then overapplies to user queries, causing hallucination or style collapse.
- Observed in backlog: many regressions post-rollout tied to novel punctuation in examples or an outlier exemplar that set an unintended policy (see linked PR #87).

Hypotheses / initial ideas
1) Exemplars that differ in superficial tokens but are semantically same create stronger robustness if we actively diversify surface cues (microcue jitter).
2) Removing the single exemplar with the strongest cue and replacing with multiple weaker exemplars improves aggregate behavior (prune-and-sprout).
3) Soft instructions (gentle system-level nudges) + lower temperature can reduce microcue overfitting without losing creativity.

Experiment matrix (fast, cheap runs)
- Models: rw-small-2024, rw-medium-quant-2024
- Prompt scaffolds: (A) minimal system + 4 exemplars; (B) system + 8 micro-variants; (C) system + 4 exemplars + explicit "diversify formatting" instruction
- Variables: exemplar_count ∈ {3,4,8}, exemplar_variants ∈ {none, jittered}, temperature ∈ {0.0, 0.3, 0.7}
- Metrics: failure_rate (manual labels), token-cost, top-1 confusion (when expected answer type is misapplied), style-drift score (embedding distance vs reference style cluster)

Quick template examples (raw, iterate)
- System: "You are a concise assistant. Follow examples, produce answer only. If unsure, say 'I don't know.'"
- Exemplar pattern (original):
  Q: "How to reset my API key?"
  A: "Go to Settings → API keys → Revoke → Create new."

- Jittered variants (surface-level changes):
  Q: "How do I rotate an API key?"
  A: "Open Settings > API keys. Revoke the old, then create a new one."

  Q: "I'm trying to rotate a key—what's the flow?"
  A: "Settings → Developer → Revoke key, Create key. Update your app."

Failure cases observed (examples copied from tests):
- Example-level overapply: model started appending "Update your app" to unrelated answers when one exemplar had that trailing phrase.
- Punctuation latch: an exemplar that used em dashes caused models to replicate em dash-heavy prose in otherwise plain answers.
- Label-swapping: an exemplar with "Answer (short):" prefix made the model output the wrong field label for different tasks.

Debugging notes (handy heuristics)
- Single-exemplar ablation: run 1-shot ablations where each exemplar is removed in turn; if failure rate drops significantly when a particular exemplar is removed, that exemplar is a microcue suspect.
- Surface-normalization ablation: normalize punctuation/whitespace in exemplars; compare behavior. If normalization helps, cue is surface-level.
- Exemplar-ensemble scoring: give a short meta-prompt that asks model to rate which exemplar seems most "similar" to the user Q; if one exemplar consistently wins, it's too dominating.

Early results (notes from 2025-02-10 quick run)
- Prune-and-sprout: removing 1 dominant exemplar and replacing with 2 jittered variants reduced the failure_rate from 12% → 6% on small synthetic set. Cost increased ~8% tokens.
- System soft-nudge + temp 0.3 lowered label-swapping but slightly increased terse "I don't know" outputs (good trade for safety).
- Normalizing punctuation (replace em-dash with simple hyphen) removed the em-dash style drift in ~80% regressions.

Open micro-experiments to try next
- Automated exemplar scaffolder: generate 3 surface variants per exemplar via simple rules (synonymize, punctuation swap, label-style swap) and test ensemble. Idea: cheap data augmentation of prompt bank.
- Slot-in adversarial exemplar: intentionally add a toxic or misleading exemplar to see if model amplifies—used as stress test. Keep offline.
- Rolling-reorder: randomize exemplar order per request (cheap shuffle) vs fixed canonical order; measure stability and cost.

Checklist / TODOs
- [ ] Write small script to run single-exemplar ablation across our 200-shot QA benchmark (ticket: PROMPT-127).
- [ ] Add punctuation-normalization preprocessor to prompt-builder.
- [ ] Add a "dominance score" to the prompt dashboard (per-exemplar activation proxy) — discuss with Priya.
- [ ] Draft short internal doc summarizing wins/losses for product team (1 pager).

Notes to reviewers
- This is messy and iterative — the intention is to capture heuristics I keep reusing. If you see redundancy, flag it; if you have a better quick-test harness, ping me (Avery).

Random musings (brain dump)
- Maybe we should build a "microcue fingerprint" feature: canonicalize small surface cues into a sparse vector and surface exemplars with similar fingerprints in the console. Could help UX teams pick diverse exemplars.
- Consider a "soft-rerank" middleware: if the model output matches a known microcue template too closely, rerank to a fallback generation pattern. Heavy, but effective for enterprise complaints.

End of scratchpad.
